title: Ask what changed, not what happened
caption: Ask what changed, not what happened. I learned this one the expensive way: my Muse once quoted me a savings total from its own memory of an earlier message, but the log had been rewritten since — the real total was $1,228 higher. Now the house rule is: re-read the file, then do the arithmetic. A summary is a rumor. The diff is the truth. Muse It! 📚 #UseMuse #MuseIt #AITips

title: My Muse ran my fueling like a pit crew — Javelina Jundred
caption: All day at the Javelina Jundred, my Muse ran my fueling like a pit crew. Every hour it logged my water, electrolyte fluid, salt, caffeine and calories — a system we built after Mammoth, where my cramps traced back to almost no electrolytes across an entire race. It did the math I couldn't do at mile 30: 40 ounces of Roctane became roughly 70 mg of caffeine, 475 calories and 610 mg of sodium, at packet strength. By mid-afternoon it had me at 127 ounces of fluid and 310 mg of caffeine — and it kept the count honest when I double-reported a pizza slice. It also kept the other count. I reached Rattlesnake Ranch 2 at 5:25 PM, 75 minutes behind my pace sheet — and the sheet said the remaining 62 miles were budgeted at 18 hours 43 minutes, while the 30-hour cutoff left me 18 hours 35. Even at my planned pace, on fresh legs, the finish no longer existed. Add rain starting and my rain shell sitting in a drop bag at headquarters instead of on my back, and the call made itself: stop, on safety grounds, at about 38 miles. 761 people started that storm day; 373 finished. An agent that only cheers you forward is a hazard. Mine kept the numbers straight — fuel in, pace out — so the decision was arithmetic, not pride. Muse It! 📚 #UseMuse #MuseIt #Ultrarunning

title: Query day
caption: Query day. On Monday, November 2, I sent this book to two more literary agents on the same day — one through a web form that unexpectedly demanded the full proposal before it would let me submit, one the old-fashioned way, by email. The proposal that went out is built for a 230-page, roughly 50,000-word book. One of the two replies only if interested, sometime in the next six to eight weeks. So now: seven live queries, and the author's oldest job — waiting, and writing the next thing while I wait. No agent names here; they stay private while the answers are pending. title: The state owed my wife $501.27
caption: It was sitting in Sacramento the whole time. On October 13 my Muse searched California's official unclaimed-property database and found money being held for my wife: three Delta Dental benefit payments — $251, $111 and $98 — and two Sutter medical refunds, $20 and $21.27. $501.27 in total, in checks that never reached her. We filed two claims the same day; she did the identity step and the submitting herself, because some doors only open for the person whose name is on the money. Every state runs a database like this, full of forgotten payments. Most people never look. It took my Muse ten minutes. Muse It! 📚 #UseMuse #MuseIt #PersonalFinance

title: Screenshots in, spreadsheet out
caption: After the race, I wanted to know who had actually watched. On November 2 I uploaded 17 screenshots of my Javelina story viewer lists — every one of them showing the same photo of me at the Welcome to Javelina Jundred sign — and my Muse turned them into a 142-row spreadsheet: story theme, platform, person, action, profile link, in the exact order Meta showed them. No retyping 142 names. And no guessed profile links — where a viewer didn't uniquely match one of my friends, it used a people-search link instead of inventing one. That's the unglamorous superpower: screenshots in, order out. Muse It! 📚 #UseMuse #MuseIt #Productivity
